source_caption:
To authentically portray the fiercely elite Agojie warriors, director Gina Prince-Bythewood absolutely refused to rely on stunt doubles or heavy CGI. Instead, she required her entire female cast, led by a 56-year-old Viola Davis, to undergo months of gruelingly intense physical training. The actors endured daily regimens of heavy weightlifting, martial arts, and complex weapons choreography so they could physically perform their own devastatingly brutal fight sequences. By demanding genuine, exhausting physical transformation, the production brilliantly proves that the most powerful on-screen warriors aren’t created in a computer lab, but forged through raw, unapologetic human sweat and absolute dedication.
⠀
The Woman King (2022), directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood, starring Viola Davis, Thuso Mbedu, Lashana Lynch. In the fiercely powerful 1820s West African kingdom of Dahomey, a battle-hardened general must heavily train a new generation of entirely female elite warriors to protect their people against a massive, deeply ruthless foreign enemy determined to destroy their way of life.

source_details.synopsis: The Woman King is a 2022 fictionalised historical drama depicting the Agojie, the all-female regiment in the West African Kingdom of Dahomey. An American action-adventure film set in the 1820s, it stars Viola Davis as a general who trains the next generation of female warriors to fight their enemies. It is directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood and written by Dana Stevens, based on a story she wrote with Maria Bello. The film also stars Thuso Mbedu, Lashana Lynch, Sheila Atim, Hero Fiennes Tiffin, and John Boyega.
